event: US restricts advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools to China
description: BIS interim final rule creates licence requirements for high-end AI and supercomputing chips and for advanced chipmaking equipment going to China. Baseline for everything that follows (predates the chart).

event: Huawei Mate 60 Pro ships with SMIC 7nm chip
description: TechInsights teardown finds the phone's Kirin 9000S is made on SMIC's 7nm (N+2) process, the first advanced-node chip from a Chinese foundry since the 2022 controls.
notes: Launch date from Caixin (the phone went on sale 2023-08-29); 7nm finding from TechInsights: https://www.techinsights.com/blog/techinsights-finds-smic-7nm-n2-huawei-mate-60-pro

event: US tightens AI chip thresholds
description: BIS adds a performance density test to the 2022 chip thresholds to stop workarounds using chips designed to sit just under the old limits. Nvidia said the rule covers its A800, H800 and L40S. Effective 2023-11-17.
notes: Nvidia's 8-K of 2023-10-17 names the A800, H800 and L40S as newly covered: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581023000217/nvda-20231017.htm

event: 13 Chinese entities added to Entity List
description: BIS adds 13 China-based entities to the Entity List alongside the chip rule update: GPU designers Biren and Moore Thread and their subsidiaries.
notes: Names confirmed in the rule text

event: US adds HBM and more chipmaking tools to controls
description: BIS interim final rule adds controls on high-bandwidth memory, more semiconductor manufacturing equipment and software, and new foreign direct product rules.

event: 140 entities added to Entity List
description: BIS adds 140 entities (China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore) and modifies 14 Chinese entries, published with the HBM and equipment rule.

event: AI Diffusion Rule issued
description: BIS 'Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion' sets worldwide licence requirements for advanced chips and, for the first time, controls on closed model weights. Published 2025-01-15.

event: Foundry due diligence rule
description: BIS adds due diligence requirements for foundries and packaging houses making advanced computing chips, aimed at Chinese designers using overseas fabs.

event: 27 entities added to Entity List
description: Two rules on the same day add 16 entities (14 China, 2 Singapore), including chip designer Sophgo and its affiliates, and 11 more Chinese entities, including model developer Zhipu AI and its subsidiaries.
notes: Names confirmed in the rule texts. Second rule (Zhipu): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm

event: Inspur subsidiaries and other AI/HPC firms added to Entity List
description: BIS adds 12 entities (11 China, 1 Taiwan) for developing advanced AI, supercomputers and high-performance AI chips for Chinese military-linked end users; reported to include six Inspur subsidiaries. A companion rule adds 70 more entities.
notes: Inspur detail is from press coverage, not the abstract

event: US requires licence for Nvidia H20 sales to China
description: US government tells Nvidia that H20 chips, designed to comply with the 2023 thresholds, need an export licence for China; on 2025-04-14 it says the requirement is indefinite. Nvidia discloses up to $5.5B in charges.

event: AI Diffusion Rule rescinded
description: BIS announces it will rescind the AI Diffusion Rule before its compliance date and issues guidance that using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere risks violating US controls.

event: US signals H20 licences will be granted
description: Nvidia says the US government has assured it that H20 licences for China will be granted, reversing April's de facto ban.

event: 23 Chinese entities added to Entity List
description: BIS adds 32 entities, 23 of them in China. They include GMC Semiconductor and Jicun Semiconductor (diverting US items to listed parties), Shanghai Fudan Microelectronics and Sino IC (high-performance computing chips, including for AI), and firms in China's advanced computing and chip manufacturing sectors. Others are biotech and aerospace.
notes: Chip relevance confirmed in the rule text

event: Huawei publishes Ascend chip roadmap
description: At Huawei Connect, Eric Xu sets out a three-year roadmap: Ascend 950PR in Q1 2026, 950DT in Q4 2026, 960 in Q4 2027, 970 in Q4 2028.

event: Affiliates (50%) rule extends Entity List reach
description: BIS applies Entity List restrictions to any company at least 50% owned by a listed entity.

event: Affiliates rule suspended for one year
description: BIS suspends the affiliates rule until 2026-11-09 as part of the US-China trade truce.
notes: Trade-truce context is from memory; the rule itself confirms the dates

event: Trump says Nvidia H200 sales to China will be allowed
description: In a Truth Social post, the President says Nvidia may ship H200 chips to approved customers in China, with 25% paid to the US government, and that Commerce is finalising the details.
notes: Reuters report of the Truth Social post, carried by Khaleej Times; the post itself was not retrieved

event: Huawei Kirin 9030 found on SMIC 5nm-class N+3
description: TechInsights finds the Mate 80 Pro Max's Kirin 9030 is made on SMIC's N+3 process using DUV multi-patterning: denser than 7nm but still behind TSMC and Samsung 5nm, with expected yield problems.
notes: Date is the SCMP article date; the TechInsights finding is a few days earlier

event: Reuters reports Chinese EUV lithography prototype
description: Reuters reports a Shenzhen lab completed a prototype EUV machine in early 2025, built by former ASML engineers. It generates EUV light but has not produced working chips.
notes: Link is a syndicated copy of the Reuters exclusive

event: US moves H200-class chips to case-by-case licensing
description: BIS changes licence review for Nvidia H200 and equivalents (and lesser chips) to China from presumption of denial to case by case, with supply, security and third-party testing conditions. Announced 2026-01-13. China's customs reportedly then blocked H200 imports.

event: Huawei Ascend 950PR heads to mass production
description: Reuters reports mass production starting April 2026, about 750,000 units planned for the year, and ByteDance and Alibaba planning orders after successful testing.
notes: Date is the report date, not a production milestone. Link is RTHK carrying the Reuters report

event: BIS: licence needed for chips to China-headquartered firms anywhere
description: BIS guidance clarifies that advanced chips need a licence when the buyer or its ultimate parent is headquartered in China, even if the buyer is located in a third country.
notes: Summary taken from law-firm write-ups of the guidance; I did not read the PDF itself
